elements.context: μὴ πάνυ τι εὐδαίμονας ποιεῖν τούτους τοὺς ἄνδρας
ἕν τι ἡμῖν ἔθνος ἔσται διαφερόντως εὔδαιμον
τοὺς ἄλλους πάντας τοιούτῳ τρόπῳ μακαρίους ποιεῖν
ἵνα δὴ ὅλη ἡ πόλις εὐδαιμονῇ

signals.observation: Forms of εὐδαίμων/εὐδαιμονία saturate the section, shifting between individual happiness (τούτους τοὺς ἄνδρας, ἕν τι ἔθνος) and whole-city happiness (ὅλη ἡ πόλις); μακάριος appears twice as a near-synonym in the lists of conventional goods.

elements.context: ὅπως ἕν τι ἡμῖν ἔθνος ἔσται διαφερόντως εὔδαιμον
ἀλλʼ ὅπως ὅτι μάλιστα ὅλη ἡ πόλις

signals.observation: A stated contrast between making one group (ἕν τι ἔθνος) exceptionally happy versus the whole city (ὅλη ἡ πόλις); ὅλην recurs at 420c and ὅλη again at 420e.
Adeimantus catalogues conventional goods denied to the guardians: land, fine houses, furnishings, private sacrifices, hosting guests, gold and silver—a cluster of possessions and private activities.

elements.context: ὥσπερ ἐπίκουροι μισθωτοὶ ἐν τῇ πόλει φαίνονται καθῆσθαι
ταῦτά γε ἐπισίτιοι καὶ οὐδὲ μισθὸν πρὸς τοῖς σιτίοις λαμβάνοντες

signals.observation: Adeimantus likens guardians to hired mercenaries (ἐπίκουροι μισθωτοί); Socrates intensifies this by adding ἐπισίτιοι—they receive only food, not even wages on top of it.

elements.context: μετρίως ἂν ἐδοκοῦμεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀπολογεῖσθαι

signals.observation: The exchange is framed as a forensic pair: κατηγορία/κατηγορέω (accusation) answered by ἀπολογέομαι (defense), recurring across the section.

elements.context: ὥσπερ οὖν ἂν εἰ ἡμᾶς ἀνδριάντα γράφοντας
οἱ γὰρ ὀφθαλμοὶ κάλλιστον ὂν οὐκ ὀστρείῳ ἐναληλιμμένοι εἶεν ἀλλὰ μέλανι

signals.observation: A statue-painting analogy: painting eyes with ὄστρειον (purple) rather than μέλαν (black) would make them cease to appear as eyes; the fairest colors (κάλλιστα φάρμακα) must suit each part, not beautify it in isolation.

elements.context: τοὺς γεωργοὺς ξυστίδας ἀμφιέσαντες καὶ χρυσὸν περιθέντες
τοὺς κεραμέας κατακλίναντες ἐπὶ δεξιὰ πρὸς τὸ πῦρ

signals.observation: Farmers and potters given luxuries would cease to be what they are; this is stated via emphatic doubling: ὁ γεωργὸς γεωργός, ὁ κεραμεὺς κεραμεύς—each noun repeated to mark the loss of identity with role.
πλοῦτος and πενία are named together at 421d as what corrupts craftsmen, then repeated together at 422a as what guardians must keep from entering the city.

elements.context: πλουτήσας χυτρεὺς δοκεῖ σοι ἔτʼ ἐθελήσειν ἐπιμελεῖσθαι τῆς τέχνης

signals.observation: χυτρεύς (potter) appears first as one enriched, then as one made worse—the same craftsman named in two stages of deterioration.

elements.context: τοῦ μὲν τρυφὴν καὶ ἀργίαν καὶ νεωτερισμὸν ἐμποιοῦντος
τῆς δὲ ἀνελευθερίαν καὶ κακοεργίαν πρὸς τῷ νεωτερισμῷ

signals.observation: Wealth produces τρυφή, ἀργία, νεωτερισμός; poverty produces ἀνελευθερία, κακοεργία, plus νεωτερισμός again—νεωτερισμός is shared by both, linking the two lists.

elements.context: φύλακες δὲ νόμων τε καὶ πόλεως

signals.observation: φύλαξ recurs densely; at 421e φυλακτέον (verbal adjective of φυλάσσω) appears alongside φύλαξιν, so the guardians' task (guarding) names what must itself be guarded against.
The guardians are described as merely sitting (καθῆσθαι) and garrisoning (φρουροῦντες)—static confinement rather than active enjoyment.
A contrast between being and seeming applied to guardians: those who are not guardians but seem to be (μὴ ὄντες ἀλλὰ δοκοῦντες) destroy the city utterly (πᾶσαν ἄρδην ἀπολλύασιν).

elements.context: ὥσπερ ἐν πανηγύρει ἀλλʼ οὐκ ἐν πόλει ἑστιάτορας εὐδαίμονας

signals.observation: Festival-goers at a πανήγυρις are contrasted with citizens in a πόλις: treating guardians as happy feasters would make the city a festival, not a polity.
Three verbal adjectives in -τέον (ἀναγκαστέον, πειστέον, ἐατέον) appear in close sequence, prescribing what must be done with guardians and city.

elements.context: καὶ τὸ τούτου ἀδελφὸν δόξω σοι μετρίως λέγειν

signals.observation: Socrates introduces the next argument as τὸ τούτου ἀδελφόν—a 'sibling' point—a striking kinship metaphor for a related argument.

sections.title: The City at War and the Limits of City Size

signals.observation: The lexical family of wealth (πλούσιος/πλουτέω) recurs densely across the section, applied to enemy soldiers, rival cities, and the internal division of cities into rich and poor.

Forms of εἷς/μία recur with exceptional density, moving from one boxer to one city-opponent to the principle that each city must be one, each citizen one person doing one work, and the whole city must grow as one.

elements.context: πόλεις εἰσὶ πάμπολλαι ἀλλʼ οὐ πόλις

signals.observation: The contrast between μία/εἷς and πολλαί/πολλοί structures the section: other cities are many-not-one, citizens must become one-not-many.

elements.context: οἱ ἀθληταὶ … διπλασίοις τε καὶ τριπλασίοις αὑτῶν μαχοῦνται
εἷς πύκτης ὡς οἷόν τε κάλλιστα ἐπὶ τοῦτο παρεσκευασμένος

signals.observation: The analogy between war and boxing is developed through a cluster of athletic vocabulary: πύκτης, πυκτική, ἀθληταί, with the trained boxer set against untrained rich opponents.

elements.context: κυσὶ πολεμεῖν στερεοῖς τε καὶ ἰσχνοῖς
μετὰ κυνῶν προβάτοις πίοσί τε καὶ ἁπαλοῖς

signals.observation: The adjective πίων first describes the fat non-boxers (πιόνοιν) and returns in the dog-sheep image (πίοσι), linking the boxer analogy to the animal analogy through shared fatness vocabulary.

The boxing tactic is described with specific physical movements: retreating (ὑποφεύγοντι), turning back (ἀναστρέφοντα), and striking (κρούειν), performed repeatedly in sun and heat (ἐν ἡλίῳ τε καὶ πνίγει).

elements.context: πόλεις εἰσὶ πάμπολλαι ἀλλʼ οὐ πόλις, τὸ τῶν παιζόντων

signals.observation: The phrase τὸ τῶν παιζόντων marks the claim that other cities are many-not-one as something said in game-playing or jest.

elements.context: μεγίστη ἔσται, οὐ τῷ εὐδοκιμεῖν λέγω, ἀλλʼ ὡς ἀληθῶς μεγίστη

signals.observation: A contrast between truly greatest (ὡς ἀληθῶς μεγίστη) and merely seeming great (δοκούσας), even with only a thousand fighters (χιλίων τῶν προπολεμούντων).

The verb φυλάττω clusters densely alongside the noun φύλαξ: the guardians are commanded to guard city size, then to guard education and music—the activity of guarding becomes their defining repeated action.

elements.context: καὶ φαῦλόν γʼ … ἴσως αὐτοῖς προστάξομεν

signals.observation: φαῦλος appears four times in quick succession: Adeimantus calls the injunction trivial (φαῦλόν), Socrates escalates with φαυλότερον, then says all tasks are φαῦλα if they guard one great thing; φαῦλος also describes a guardian's inferior offspring.

elements.context: μέχρι οὗ ἂν ἐθέλῃ αὐξομένη εἶναι μία, μέχρι τούτου αὔξειν, πέρα δὲ μή

signals.observation: The limit (ὅρος) of city size is stated as a repeated μέχρι construction with a sharp cutoff (πέρα δὲ μή), the boundary defined by willingness to remain one.
αὐξάνω appears for city growth (limited by unity) and then for the virtuous cycle of education (ἔρχεται ὥσπερ κύκλος αὐξανομένη)—growth recurs in two different structures, one bounded, one circular.

elements.context: ὥς φησί τε Δάμων καὶ ἐγὼ πείθομαι

signals.observation: Socrates says he is persuaded (πείθομαι) by Damon's claim about music and political laws; Adeimantus immediately asks to be placed among the persuaded (πεπεισμένων), the section ending on a transfer of persuasion.
μουσικῆς τρόποι (modes/ways of music) are said never to change without the greatest πολιτικῶν νόμων changing—νόμος itself carrying the double sense of law and musical mode.
παιδεία and τροφή appear paired: first as the one great thing to guard, then reversed in order (τροφὴ καὶ παίδευσις) as the mechanism of the virtuous cycle.
Socrates calls the one thing μέγα, then immediately corrects himself: not μέγα but ἱκανόν—replacing greatness with sufficiency as the proper term.

elements.context: ἡμεῖς μὲν οὐδὲν χρυσίῳ οὐδʼ ἀργυρίῳ χρώμεθα

signals.observation: The proposed embassy declares the city's non-use of gold and silver as θέμις (divine law/custom), offering allied war spoils in exchange—a diplomatic speech embedded within the argument.

sections.title: Music as Fortress, Lawful Play, and Deferring Religion to Apollo

signals.observation: παρανομία's progress is described through a dense chain of directional verbs: slipping in (παραδυομένη), settling in (εἰσοικισαμένη), flowing beneath (ὑπορρεῖ), stepping out larger (ἐκβαίνει), going toward laws (ἔρχεται), and overturning everything (ἀνατρέψῃ).
The νόμος root recurs across παρανομία, παράνομος, ἔννομος (twice), and εὐνομία, shifting from lawlessness to lawfulness within the discussion of play and music.
παιδιά (play) and παῖς/παίζειν (child/to play) cluster together; play is first dismissed as harmless, then required to be lawful, then children are shown playing their way into εὐνομία.
The guardpost (φυλακτήριον) must be built (οἰκοδομητέον) for the guardians (φύλαξιν) — a building metaphor placed in music.

συμβόλαιον recurs four times across the section: first as the stage lawlessness reaches, then as the marketplace contracts Socrates refuses to legislate, then as the site of fraud the Hydra-cutters try to fix.

elements.context: τοὺς κάμνοντάς τε καὶ οὐκ ἐθέλοντας
ποικιλώτερα καὶ μείζω ποιοῦσι τὰ νοσήματα
οὔτε φάρμακα οὔτε καύσεις οὔτε τομαί

signals.observation: A medical cluster: the sick who won't change their regimen are treated with an escalating list — φάρμακα, καύσεις, τομαί, ἐπῳδαί, περίαπτα — none of which help. The city is then compared to them.

elements.context: θεῶν τε καὶ δαιμόνων καὶ ἡρώων θεραπεῖαι

signals.observation: θεραπεία/θεραπεύω appears in four distinct contexts: care of parents, flattering a badly governed city, willingness to serve such cities, and service to gods, daimons, and heroes.

elements.context: ἐπανορθοῦσα εἴ τι καὶ πρότερον τῆς πόλεως ἔκειτο
πολλὰ τοιαῦτα τιθέμενοι ἀεὶ καὶ ἐπανορθούμενοι
νομοθετοῦντές τε οἷα ἄρτι διήλθομεν καὶ ἐπανορθοῦντες

signals.observation: ἐπανορθόω appears three times: first as genuine correction from εὐνομία, then twice for the futile correcting done by those who endlessly legislate.

χαρίεις/χάρις/χαρίζομαι cluster densely: χαριέντως is used ironically of the sick, χαρίεν denied of their anger at truth-tellers, χάριν absent from anger at good advice, χαρίζηται describes flattering bad cities, and χαριέστατοι is ironic of endless legislators.
The Hydra appears as a simile for the futility of cutting at problems through piecemeal legislation — a striking singleton.
A four-part list of what the sick person must cease: drinking, gorging, sexual indulgence, idleness — presented as the true prerequisite before any remedy can help.
μουσική is first the location where the guardpost is built and then the channel through which εὐνομία is received.

elements.context: τῷ μέντοι Ἀπόλλωνι τῷ ἐν Δελφοῖς
πάτριος ἐξηγητὴς ἐν μέσῳ τῆς γῆς ἐπὶ τοῦ ὀμφαλοῦ καθήμενος

signals.observation: Apollo at Delphi is called the ancestral interpreter (πάτριος ἐξηγητής), described as seated at the navel of the earth (ἐν μέσῳ τῆς γῆς ἐπὶ τοῦ ὀμφαλοῦ), and assigned the greatest, finest, and first legislation.

elements.context: σιγάς τε τῶν νεωτέρων παρὰ πρεσβυτέροις

signals.observation: A list of small social customs — silences, reclining, rising, care of parents, haircuts, cloaks, shoes, bodily bearing — presented as things discovered naturally by the well-educated rather than legislated.

elements.context: οὐκ ἂν ἔτι τὰ τοιαῦτα ἐπιχειρήσαιμι νομοθετεῖν
τί ἂν ἡμῖν λοιπὸν τῆς νομοθεσίας

signals.observation: νομοθετέω and its cognates recur throughout: legislating small things is called foolish, Socrates refuses to attempt it, endless legislators are mocked, the true lawgiver abstains, and the remaining νομοθεσία is deferred to Apollo.

elements.context: εἰς ἕν τι τέλεον καὶ νεανικὸν ἀποβαίνειν αὐτὸ ἢ ἀγαθὸν ἢ καὶ τοὐναντίον

signals.observation: Like calls to like (τὸ ὅμοιον ὅμοιον παρακαλεῖ), and the process ends in something complete and vigorous (τέλεον καὶ νεανικόν) — either good or its opposite.

sections.title: The City Declared Founded; The Search for Wisdom

signals.observation: Four forms of οἰκίζω appear across the section, marking the city as already founded at the opening and returning at each stage of the search.
The search for justice in the city is introduced with an instruction to procure sufficient light (φῶς) from somewhere.

elements.context: ἐάν πως ἴδωμεν ποῦ ποτʼ ἂν εἴη ἡ δικαιοσύνη
πρῶτόν γέ μοι δοκεῖ ἐν αὐτῷ κατάδηλον εἶναι ἡ σοφία

signals.observation: Visibility language clusters around the search: seeing (ἴδωμεν), being plainly visible (κατάδηλον), and appearing (φαίνεται).

elements.context: ὅτι ἂν αὐτῶν εὕρωμεν ἐν αὐτῇ

signals.observation: Forms of εὑρίσκω frame the section: anticipated finding at the start, claimed finding at the close.

elements.context: ἡ εὐβουλία, δῆλον ὅτι ἐπιστήμη τίς ἐστιν
ἔστι τις ἐπιστήμη ἐν τῇ ἄρτι ὑφʼ ἡμῶν οἰκισθείσῃ

signals.observation: ἐπιστήμη recurs densely as various craft-knowledges are tested and rejected before the guardians' knowledge is identified.

elements.form: καρποῦ τῆς γενέσεως ἐκ τῆς γῆς

signals.observation: A sequence of craft-knowledges (carpentry, bronze-work, farming) is rejected before φυλακική is accepted; each is named by its material or product.

elements.context: μὴ οὐ βοηθεῖν δικαιοσύνῃ εἰς δύναμιν παντὶ τρόπῳ

signals.observation: Glaucon reminds Socrates of his promise (ὑπέσχου) to search, characterizing failure to help justice as impious (οὐχ ὅσιον).
Socrates requests joint participation (συλλαμβάνειν) and Glaucon immediately accepts with a future commitment (ποιήσομεν).

elements.form: τὸ ὑπόλοιπον ἔσται τὸ οὐχ ηὑρημένον

signals.observation: A method of residues is stated: finding three of four items identifies the fourth as the remainder (τὸ ὑπολειφθέν).
The city is called wise as a whole (ὅλη) through its smallest group and part (σμικροτάτῳ ἔθνει καὶ μέρει).

elements.context: πάντων τούτων οὗτοι ἂν εἶεν ὀλίγιστοι

signals.observation: The superlative ὀλίγιστος appears twice in close succession, emphasizing the fewness of the guardians.
The first found virtue is described as seated or established (ἵδρυται) somewhere in the city, giving it a spatial location within the πόλις.

elements.context: ἡ εὐβουλία, δῆλον ὅτι ἐπιστήμη τίς ἐστιν

signals.observation: εὔβουλος/εὐβουλία mediates between σοφία and ἐπιστήμη: the city is wise because well-counselled, and good counsel is a knowledge.

elements.context: ἐάντε λανθάνῃ ἐάντε μὴ πάντας θεούς τε καὶ ἀνθρώπους

signals.observation: Whether justice is hidden or not from all gods and humans (λανθάνῃ) is posed as irrelevant to the question of possessing it for happiness.
Wisdom is said to involve something strange (ἄτοπον), flagged before the explanation that the city's wisdom belongs to its fewest members.

elements.context: διὰ παντὸς σώσει τὴν περὶ τῶν δεινῶν δόξαν
σωτηρίαν ἔγωγʼ λέγω τινὰ εἶναι τὴν ἀνδρείαν
διὰ παντὸς δὲ ἔλεγον αὐτῆς σωτηρίαν
τὸ ἔν τε λύπαις ὄντα διασῴζεσθαι αὐτήν

signals.observation: The σῴζω/σωτηρία family recurs densely: courage is defined as σωτηρία, the capacity σώσει the δόξα, one must διασῴζεσθαι it through adversity, and the final definition restates σωτηρίαν.
βάπτω/βαφή forms saturate the dyeing analogy and then transfer to the education of soldiers, where laws are received ὥσπερ βαφήν.

elements.context: ἵνα δευσοποιὸς αὐτῶν ἡ δόξα γίγνοιτο

signals.observation: δευσοποιός appears first of the dyed wool, then of the soldiers' δόξα — the quality of being fast-dyed transfers from craft object to opinion.

elements.context: οὔτʼ ἄνευ ῥυμμάτων οὔτε μετὰ ῥυμμάτων
μὴ αὐτῶν ἐκπλύναι τὴν βαφὴν τὰ ῥύμματα ταῦτα

signals.observation: ῥύμμα recurs three times, shifting from literal detergents to the metaphorical solvents (pleasure, pain, fear, desire) that wash out the dye of correct opinion.

elements.context: τὸ ἔν τε λύπαις ὄντα διασῴζεσθαι
λύπη τε καὶ φόβος καὶ ἐπιθυμία

signals.observation: The fourfold list λύπη, ἡδονή, ἐπιθυμία, φόβος appears first as dative plurals (conditions to endure) and returns as nominative singulars (ῥύμματα that wash out the dye), with ἡδονή promoted to leading position and singled out as most dangerous.

elements.context: ἐκλέγονται ἐκ τοσούτων χρωμάτων μίαν φύσιν τὴν τῶν λευκῶν

signals.observation: ἐκλέγω is used first of dyers selecting white wool, then of the city selecting soldiers — the same verb bridges the analogy.

elements.context: σώσει τὴν περὶ τῶν δεινῶν δόξαν
τὴν τῆς δόξης τῆς ὑπὸ νόμου
σωτηρίαν διὰ παντὸς δόξης ὀρθῆς τε καὶ νομίμου
τὴν ὀρθὴν δόξαν περὶ τῶν αὐτῶν τούτων ἄνευ παιδείας

signals.observation: δόξα recurs throughout as the object that courage preserves; in the final exchange it is qualified as ὀρθή but ἄνευ παιδείας, which is excluded from ἀνδρεία.

elements.context: τὰ ῥύμματα ταῦτα, δεινὰ ὄντα ἐκκλύζειν

signals.observation: δεινός shifts between 'terrible things' (the object of correct opinion) and 'terrible/formidable' as a description of the ῥύμματα themselves, especially ἡδονή called δεινοτέρα.
Three washing-out compounds cluster: ἔκπλυτα describes poorly dyed wool, ἐκπλύναι the risk to soldiers' dye, and ἐκκλύζειν the action of the ῥύμματα.
Correct opinion without παιδεία is called θηριώδη καὶ ἀνδραποδώδη and excluded as οὔτε νόμιμον — contrasted with the νόμιμος δόξα that constitutes genuine ἀνδρεία.
The dyeing analogy emphasizes prior preparation with compound forms: προπαρασκευάζουσιν, παρασκευῇ, and the negative condition μὴ προθεραπεύσας.
Socrates qualifies the accepted ἀνδρεία as πολιτικήν and defers a fuller (κάλλιον) treatment, marking the present finding as provisional.

elements.context: νῦν γὰρ οὐ τοῦτο ἐζητοῦμεν, ἀλλὰ δικαιοσύνην

signals.observation: The section closes by naming δικαιοσύνη as the actual object of the search, subordinating the just-completed account of ἀνδρεία to it.

elements.context: εἰς τοῦτο τὸ μέρος ὃ προπολεμεῖ τε καὶ στρατεύεται
ἀνδρεία ἄρα πόλις μέρει τινὶ ἑαυτῆς ἐστι

signals.observation: μέρος appears twice to locate courage in a specific part of the city — the part that fights on its behalf.
Poorly dyed wool is called γελοῖα — laughable/ridiculous — applied to the result of dyeing without proper preparation.

sections.title: Temperance as Harmony Throughout the City

elements.context: δύο μήν … ἃ δεῖ κατιδεῖν ἐν τῇ πόλει
ἀπόβλεπε τοίνυν πρὸς τὴν νέαν ἡμῖν πόλιν
οὐκοῦν καὶ ταῦτα ὁρᾷς ἐνόντα σοι ἐν τῇ πόλει
τὰ μὲν τρία ἡμῖν ἐν τῇ πόλει κατῶπται

signals.observation: Repeated verbs of seeing/looking (κατιδεῖν, ἀπόβλεπε, ὁρᾷς twice, κατῶπται) structure the investigation; κατιδεῖν at the start and κατῶπται at the close share the same lemma with changed prefix-aspect.

elements.context: χείρονός τε καὶ ἀμείνονος κατὰ φύσιν συμφωνίαν

signals.observation: A musical-harmonic cluster: συμφωνία and ἁρμονία introduced together early, then ἁρμονία returns, and the conclusion adds συνᾴδοντας, συμφωνίαν, and ὁμόνοιαν, accumulating concord-language around σωφροσύνη.

elements.context: κρείττω γὰρ αὐτὴν αὑτῆς δικαίως φήσεις
κρείττω ἡδονῶν τε καὶ ἐπιθυμιῶν καὶ αὐτὴν αὑτῆς

signals.observation: κρείττω αὑτοῦ is first introduced as common parlance, then called γελοῖον, then redeployed for the city as κρείττω αὑτῆς and finally κρείττω ἡδονῶν—the phrase is rescued after being declared absurd.

elements.context: τὸ μὲν βέλτιον ἔνι, τὸ δὲ χεῖρον
χείρονός τε καὶ ἀμείνονος κατὰ φύσιν συμφωνίαν

signals.observation: Paired better/worse contrasts (βέλτιον/χεῖρον, then ἄμεινον/χείρονος) recur, shifting from soul to city; at 432a the pair χείρονος/ἀμείνονος appears inside the concluding συμφωνία formulation.

elements.context: τάς γε πολλὰς καὶ παντοδαπὰς ἐπιθυμίας
κρατουμένας αὐτόθι τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τὰς ἐν τοῖς πολλοῖς

signals.observation: ἐπιθυμία recurs four times, consistently paired with ἡδονή or with mastery language (ἐγκράτεια, κρατουμένας, κρείττω).

elements.context: ἡ ἀνδρεία καὶ ἡ σοφία ἐν μέρει τινὶ ἑκατέρα ἐνοῦσα

elements.form: διʼ ὅλης ἀτεχνῶς τέταται διὰ πασῶν

signals.observation: Σωφροσύνη is contrasted with ἀνδρεία and σοφία: each of the latter resides ἐν μέρει τινί, while σωφροσύνη is stretched διʼ ὅλης … διὰ πασῶν.
Forms of ἄρχω accumulate: first the better part rules, then rulers and ruled share a δόξα about who should rule, and the section closes with ὁπότερον δεῖ ἄρχειν as the content of the concord.
Glaucon locates σωφρονεῖν in both rulers and ruled (ἐν ἀμφοτέροις), answering Socrates' either/or question and providing the basis for the harmony claim that follows.

elements.context: πῶς οὖν ἂν τὴν δικαιοσύνην εὕροιμεν
δῆλον γὰρ ὅτι τοῦτʼ ἐστὶν ἡ δικαιοσύνη

signals.observation: The section opens naming two remaining virtues—σωφροσύνη and δικαιοσύνη—and closes with δικαιοσύνη identified as the single λοιπὸν εἶδος still to be found.

elements.context: ἄλλα ἄττα τοιαῦτα ὥσπερ ἴχνη αὐτῆς λέγεται

signals.observation: The common saying κρείττω αὑτοῦ is called an ἴχνος (trace/track) of σωφροσύνη—a concrete tracking image applied to a popular expression.

elements.context: ἐν τοῖς πολλοῖς τε καὶ φαύλοις
ἐν ὀλίγοις τε ἐπιτεύξῃ καὶ τοῖς βέλτιστα μὲν φῦσιν

elements.form: τοὺς ἀσθενεστάτους … τοὺς ἰσχυροτάτους καὶ τοὺς μέσους

signals.observation: A many/few contrast (πολλοῖς καὶ φαύλοις vs. ὀλίγοις βέλτιστα φῦσιν) is later reconfigured into a tripartite scale: ἀσθενεστάτους, ἰσχυροτάτους, μέσους, all singing together.

elements.context: ἐπιεικῶς ἐμαντευόμεθα ἄρτι ὡς ἁρμονίᾳ τινὶ ἡ σωφροσύνη ὡμοίωται

signals.observation: Socrates uses ἐμαντευόμεθα to mark that the earlier likening of σωφροσύνη to ἁρμονία (430e) has now been confirmed—a divination verb applied to his own earlier conjecture.

elements.context: τὸ βέλτιον φύσει τοῦ χείρονος ἐγκρατὲς ᾖ

signals.observation: The κρατ- root appears in ἐγκράτεια, ἐγκρατές, κρατηθῇ, and κρατουμένας, shifting between active mastery and passive being-mastered across soul and city contexts.

sections.title: The Hunt for Justice and Its Discovery in the City

elements.context: ὥσπερ κυνηγέτας τινὰς θάμνον κύκλῳ περιίστασθαι

signals.observation: A hunt cluster: hunters surrounding a thicket, justice as quarry that might escape (διαφύγῃ), a track found, and the quarry unlikely to escape (ἐκφευξεῖσθαι). Two different compounds of φεύγω frame the hunt sequence.
Dense cluster of seeing-verbs: κατιδεῖν, ἴδῃς, καθορᾶν, κατιδών mark successful or invited sight, while ἑωρῶμεν (negated), ἀπεβλέπομεν (negated), and ἀπεσκοποῦμεν mark misdirected looking.
The place where justice is hunted is described as hard to traverse, shadowy, dark, and hard to search through—four descriptors in rapid succession characterizing the terrain.

elements.context: πρὸ ποδῶν ἡμῖν ἐξ ἀρχῆς κυλινδεῖσθαι

signals.observation: Justice was rolling at their feet (πρὸ ποδῶν) while they were looking far off (πόρρω)—an explicit spatial contrast between near and far.

elements.context: λέγοντες αὐτὸ καὶ ἀκούοντες πάλαι οὐ μανθάνειν

signals.observation: Repeated forms of λέγω mark that they had been saying (ἐλέγομεν, εἰρήκαμεν) the definition of justice without recognizing it—saying without understanding.

elements.context: ὥσπερ οἱ ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν ἔχοντες ζητοῦσιν ἐνίοτε ὃ ἔχουσιν

signals.observation: Analogy of people searching for what they already hold in their hands, applied to the searchers' relation to justice.

elements.context: τὸ τὰ αὑτοῦ πράττειν καὶ μὴ πολυπραγμονεῖν δικαιοσύνη ἐστί

elements.form: τὸ αὑτοῦ ἕκαστος εἷς ὢν ἔπραττε

elements.context: ἑκάστου τούτων τὸ αὑτοῦ πράττοντος ἐν πόλει

signals.observation: The formula τὰ αὑτοῦ πράττειν recurs as the candidate definition of justice, appearing at least four times across the section.
πολυπραγμονεῖν/πολυπραγμοσύνη recurs as the antithesis of justice (τὰ αὑτοῦ πράττειν), moving from negated verb to noun naming the city's destruction.

elements.context: ἆρά σοι ἄν τι δοκεῖ μέγα βλάψαι πόλιν; οὐ πάνυ
εἰς τὸ τοῦ πολεμικοῦ εἶδος ἐπιχειρῇ ἰέναι

signals.observation: Interchange among craftsmen causes little harm (οὐ πάνυ), but interchange among the three classes (χρηματιστής into πολεμικός/φύλαξ) is ὄλεθρος—an explicit contrast in degree of damage.

elements.context: ὥσπερ ἐκ πυρείων ἐκλάμψαι ποιήσαιμεν τὴν δικαιοσύνην

signals.observation: Fire-stick image: rubbing city and individual together as fire-sticks to make justice flash forth (ἐκλάμψαι). Contrasts the earlier σκοτεινός terrain.

elements.form: πάλιν ἐπανιόντες ἐπὶ τὴν πόλιν βασανιοῦμεν

signals.observation: A back-and-forth method is described: carrying findings to the individual (ἐπαναφέρωμεν εἰς τὸν ἕνα), then returning to the city (ἐπανιόντες ἐπὶ τὴν πόλιν) to test them—both compounds of ἐπι-/ἀνα-.

elements.context: ἡ ὁμοδοξία τῶν ἀρχόντων τε καὶ ἀρχομένων
δόξης ἐννόμου σωτηρία ἐν τοῖς στρατιώταις
ἐν τοῖς ἄρχουσι φρόνησίς τε καὶ φυλακή

signals.observation: The three previously found virtues reappear compressed as σωφροσύνη (ὁμοδοξία of rulers and ruled), ἀνδρεία (σωτηρία of lawful opinion in soldiers), and σοφία (φρόνησις and φυλακή in rulers), set against justice as the rival fourth.

elements.context: κακουργίαν δὲ τὴν μεγίστην τῆς ἑαυτοῦ πόλεως οὐκ ἀδικίαν φήσεις εἶναι

signals.observation: οἰκειοπραγία is set as the direct contrary of κακουργία, which is then identified as ἀδικία—a chain: minding one's own = justice, its opposite (κακουργία) = injustice.
Glaucon casts himself as follower (ἑπομένῳ), Socrates says follow (ἕπου), Glaucon responds with lead (ἡγοῦ)—a quick exchange assigning leader/follower roles in the hunt.

elements.context: φανερὸν γὰρ δὴ ὅτι ταύτῃ πῃ ἔστιν

signals.observation: Justice risks becoming invisible (ἀφανισθεῖσα) near the section's start, is said to be evidently somewhere (φανερόν), and at the close will be made manifest (φανερὰν γενομένην)—the root φαν- tracks visibility across the section.

sections.title: Applying the City's Model to the Individual Soul

elements.context: ἀνόμοιον τυγχάνει ὂν ταύτῃ ᾗ ταὐτὸν προσαγορεύεται, ἢ ὅμοιον

signals.observation: ὅμοιος appears four times in rapid succession at 435a–b, with ἀνόμοιον posed as the rejected alternative; the cluster establishes likeness between larger and smaller as the operative relation.

elements.context: εἴδη ἐν τῇ αὑτοῦ ψυχῇ ἔχοντα
κατʼ αὐτὸ τὸ τῆς δικαιοσύνης εἶδος
τὰ αὐτὰ ἐν ἑκάστῳ ἔνεστιν ἡμῶν εἴδη τε καὶ ἤθη

signals.observation: εἶδος first names the single form of justice (435b), then shifts to plural εἴδη for the three kinds in the soul (435c, 435e).
The larger/smaller pair (μεῖζόν/ἔλαττον) frames the transfer from city to individual, with τὸν ἕνα explicitly naming the single person as the smaller counterpart.

elements.context: εἴτε ἔχει τὰ τρία εἴδη ταῦτα ἐν αὑτῇ
εἰ τῷ αὐτῷ τούτῳ ἕκαστα πράττομεν ἢ τρισὶν οὖσιν

signals.observation: Threeness recurs: τριττὰ γένη in the city, τρία εἴδη as a question about the soul, τρισὶν as the operative possibility for distinct faculties.

elements.context: εἰς φαῦλόν γε αὖ ... σκέμμα ἐμπεπτώκαμεν
οὐ πάνυ μοι δοκοῦμεν εἰς φαῦλον

signals.observation: Socrates calls the inquiry φαῦλον (easy/trivial) and is immediately contradicted: οὐ πάνυ … εἰς φαῦλον, followed by χαλεπὰ τὰ καλά.
χαλεπός appears four times, shifting from proverbial (χαλεπὰ τὰ καλά) to denied (οὐδὲν χαλεπόν) to reasserted (τόδε δὲ ἤδη χαλεπόν, τὰ χαλεπά).

elements.context: οὐ γάρ που ἄλλοθεν ἐκεῖσε ἀφῖκται

elements.form: ἐκ τῶν ἰδιωτῶν ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν ἐγγεγονέναι

signals.observation: The direction of origin runs from individuals into the city (ἐκ τῶν ἰδιωτῶν … ἐγγεγονέναι); qualities arrive there (ἐκεῖσε ἀφῖκται) from no other source (ἄλλοθεν).
Three soul-qualities are matched to geographical peoples: θυμοειδές to Thrace/Scythia, φιλομαθές to 'our region,' φιλοχρήματον to Phoenicians/Egyptians.
τόπος appears twice: the 'upper region' (τὸν ἄνω τόπον) for spiritedness, and 'the region among us' (τὸν παρʼ ἡμῖν τόπον) for love of learning.

elements.context: ἄλλη γὰρ μακροτέρα καὶ πλείων ὁδὸς ἡ ἐπὶ τοῦτο ἄγουσα
ἐκ τοιούτων μεθόδων, οἵαις νῦν ἐν τοῖς λόγοις χρώμεθα

signals.observation: Socrates distinguishes current methods (μεθόδων) from another longer road (μακροτέρα … ὁδός) that leads to precision, declaring the present approach will never yield exactness (ἀκριβῶς … οὐ μή ποτε λάβωμεν).
Three first-person plural verbs name the three psychic activities — learning, being spirited, desiring — each assigned to a different faculty (ἑτέρῳ … ἄλλῳ … τρίτῳ τινί).

elements.context: περὶ τὴν τροφήν τε καὶ γέννησιν ἡδονῶν

signals.observation: Appetite is specified through nourishment (τροφή) and generation (γέννησις) and their pleasures, with kindred desires called ἀδελφά.

elements.context: ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ καθʼ ἕκαστον αὐτῶν πράττομεν

signals.observation: The core question is posed as a disjunction: do we act with the whole soul (ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ) or with three distinct parts (τρισὶν … ἄλλο ἄλλῳ)?

elements.context: ἄλλʼ ἄττα πάθη τε καὶ ἕξεις

signals.observation: πάθη first appears paired with ἕξεις describing the city's virtues, then recurs alone when transferred to the individual soul.

sections.title: Reason and Desire Distinguished by the Principle of Opposites

elements.context: τἀναντία πάθοι ἢ καὶ εἴη ἢ καὶ ποιήσειεν
πάντα τὰ τοιαῦτα τῶν ἐναντίων ἀλλήλοις

signals.observation: Forms of ἐναντίος recur densely across the section, framing the principle at 436b, restated at 437a, applied to pairs at 437b, to desires at 437c, and to soul-conflict at 439b.

elements.context: ἑστάναι καὶ κινεῖσθαι τὸ αὐτὸ ἅμα
ἑστάναι καὶ κινεῖσθαι τὸ αὐτὸ ἅμα

signals.observation: Standing and moving are the first concrete pair of opposites used to illustrate the principle, introduced as a question about simultaneous possibility.

elements.context: οἵ γε στρόβιλοι ὅλοι ἑστᾶσί τε ἅμα καὶ κινοῦνται
ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ πήξαντες τὸ κέντρον περιφέρωνται
ἔχειν αὐτὰ εὐθύ τε καὶ περιφερὲς ἐν αὑτοῖς
εὐθύ τε καὶ περιφερὲς ἐν αὑτοῖς

signals.observation: The spinning-top example distinguishes the straight (axis) from the circular (circumference) within a single body, resolving apparent contradiction by identifying different aspects.
Four directional inclinations—right, left, forward, backward—are listed as conditions under which the spinning top can no longer be said to stand still.

elements.context: τὸ ἐφίεσθαί τινος λαβεῖν τῷ ἀπαρνεῖσθαι

signals.observation: Three paired opposites—nodding/refusing, reaching/rejecting, drawing-toward/pushing-away—are listed as examples of contrary actions or affections.

elements.context: τῶν ἐναντίων ἀλλήλοις θείης εἴτε ποιημάτων εἴτε παθημάτων

signals.observation: The infinitives ποιεῖν/πάσχειν in the principle's first statement return as the nominals ποιημάτων/παθημάτων when the three opposed pairs are classified.

elements.context: διψῆν καὶ πεινῆν καὶ ὅλως τὰς ἐπιθυμίας
ἥν τε δίψαν καλοῦμεν καὶ ἣν πεῖναν

signals.observation: Thirst and hunger recur as the most vivid (ἐναργεστάτας) instances of desire, with thirst becoming the sustained example through 439a where it is paired with its natural object, drink.

elements.context: τὸ ἀβουλεῖν καὶ μὴ ἐθέλειν μηδʼ ἐπιθυμεῖν

signals.observation: Willing/wishing are grouped with desire at 437b, then their negations (ἀβουλεῖν, μὴ ἐθέλειν, μηδʼ ἐπιθυμεῖν) are classed with pushing-away and driving-off at 437c.

elements.context: εἴ ποτέ τι αὐτὴν ἀνθέλκει διψῶσαν
τοῦ διψῶντος καὶ ἄγοντος ὥσπερ θηρίον ἐπὶ τὸ πιεῖν

signals.observation: The thirsting part leads (ἄγοντος) the soul like a beast (θηρίον) toward drink, while something else pulls it back (ἀνθέλκει)—opposed pulling forces within the soul.

elements.context: ἄγοντος ὥσπερ θηρίον ἐπὶ τὸ πιεῖν

signals.observation: The desiring element is compared to a beast (θηρίον) being led to drink—a singular image in the section.

elements.context: αἱ χεῖρες τὸ τόξον ἀπωθοῦνταί τε καὶ προσέλκονται

signals.observation: The archer analogy assigns pushing-away and drawing-toward to different hands (ἄλλη … ἑτέρα), paralleling the soul's distinct parts.

Within the soul of those who thirst but refuse to drink, a commanding element (τὸ κελεῦον) and a preventing element (τὸ κωλῦον) are distinguished as different and the latter masters the former (κρατοῦν τοῦ κελεύοντος).

elements.context: τὰ δὲ ἄγοντα καὶ ἕλκοντα διὰ παθημάτων τε καὶ νοσημάτων

signals.observation: The preventing element arises from reasoning (λογισμοῦ); the leading-and-dragging elements arrive through affections and diseases (παθημάτων, νοσημάτων).

elements.context: τὸ μὲν ᾧ λογίζεται λογιστικὸν προσαγορεύοντες τῆς ψυχῆς
τὸ δὲ ᾧ ἐρᾷ τε καὶ πεινῇ καὶ διψῇ … ἀλόγιστόν τε καὶ ἐπιθυμητικόν

signals.observation: The two parts are named: the reasoning part (λογιστικόν) and the irrational-desiring part (ἀλόγιστον καὶ ἐπιθυμητικόν), the latter characterized as companion of fillings and pleasures (πληρώσεών τινων καὶ ἡδονῶν ἑταῖρον).
Four members of the λόγος family cluster in 439d: λογισμοῦ, λογίζεται, λογιστικόν, and its privative ἀλόγιστον naming the desiring part.
The desiring part is called companion (ἑταῖρον) of certain fillings and pleasures—a social/relational term applied to a part of the soul.

elements.form: κατὰ ταὐτόν γε καὶ πρὸς ταὐτόν

elements.context: τὸ αὐτὸ ἅμα κατὰ τὸ αὐτό

elements.form: κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ πρὸς τὸ αὐτό
elements.context: ἅμα κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ πρὸς τὸ αὐτὸ τἀναντία

signals.observation: The qualifying phrase κατὰ ταὐτόν / πρὸς ταὐτόν is progressively restated and tightened across the section's formulations of the principle.

elements.context: ἔμαθον, ἔφη, καί μοι δοκεῖ οὕτως ἔχειν

signals.observation: Glaucon's οὐκ ἔμαθον prompts Socrates' οὐκ ἔμαθες and a second εἰ ἄρα νῦν ἔμαθες, finally completed by Glaucon's ἔμαθον at 438e—a failure-to-understand resolved within the section.

sections.title: The Spirited Part Distinguished; The Story of Leontius

elements.context: Λεόντιος ὁ Ἀγλαΐωνος ἀνιὼν ἐκ Πειραιῶς

signals.observation: Leontius is moving upward out of the Piraeus, an explicit directional movement.

elements.context: ἅμα δὲ αὖ δυσχεραίνοι καὶ ἀποτρέποι ἑαυτόν

signals.observation: Simultaneous desire to see and self-turning-away, marked by ἅμα μὲν … ἅμα δέ.

elements.context: τέως μὲν μάχοιτό τε καὶ παρακαλύπτοιτο

signals.observation: Fighting and covering/veiling oneself appear together as simultaneous actions of internal resistance.
Leontius physically pulls open his own eyes—a striking bodily action of forcing sight upon himself.

elements.context: ἰδοὺ ὑμῖν, ἔφη, ὦ κακοδαίμονες, ἐμπλήσθητε τοῦ καλοῦ θεάματος

signals.observation: Leontius addresses his own eyes as 'ὦ κακοδαίμονες' and commands them to be sated with the 'καλοῦ θεάματος'—the beautiful spectacle applied to corpses.

elements.context: κρατούμενος δʼ οὖν ὑπὸ τῆς ἐπιθυμίας
βιάζωνταί τινα παρὰ τὸν λογισμὸν ἐπιθυμίαι

signals.observation: The ἐπιθυμία/ἐπιθυμητικός family recurs densely across the section.

elements.context: τὴν ὀργὴν πολεμεῖν ἐνίοτε ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις
σύμμαχον τῷ λόγῳ γιγνόμενον τὸν θυμόν
τίθεσθαι τὰ ὅπλα πρὸς τὸ λογιστικόν

signals.observation: A cluster of military/political-conflict vocabulary (war, faction, alliance, arms) applied to parts of the soul.
The dog-shepherd simile appears for thumos called back by reason, then Glaucon immediately connects it to the guardians-as-dogs under ruler-shepherds in the city.
The ἐπίκουρος family links the auxiliaries in the city to thumos as natural auxiliary of the rational part.

elements.context: ὅσῳ ἂν γενναιότερος ᾖ, τοσούτῳ ἧττον δύναται ὀργίζεσθαι

signals.observation: γενναῖος appears first where nobility restrains anger at just suffering, then where the spirited part persists in 'noble efforts' against injustice.
Children and beasts are cited as evidence that thumos exists without reason—children full of θυμός from birth, some never partaking of λογισμός.

elements.form: στῆθος δὲ πλήξας κραδίην ἠνίπαπε μύθῳ

signals.observation: A Homeric quotation (Od. 20.17) where striking the chest and rebuking the heart with speech is cited as evidence of one part rebuking another.

elements.context: τὸ ἀναλογισάμενον περὶ τοῦ βελτίονός τε καὶ χείρονος

signals.observation: ἀναλογισάμενον (having reasoned) and ἀλογίστως (without reason) appear in direct contrast, sharing the λόγος root in opposed forms.

elements.context: ἐν τῇ τῆς ψυχῆς στάσει τίθεσθαι τὰ ὅπλα πρὸς τὸ λογιστικόν

signals.observation: στάσις recurs: first as faction between two warring parties, then as the soul's civil strife in which thumos takes up arms on reason's side.

elements.context: ἐὰν μὴ ὑπὸ κακῆς τροφῆς διαφθαρῇ

signals.observation: Thumos is naturally an ally of reason unless corrupted by bad rearing—a conditional qualification on the tripartite alignment.

sections.title: The Individual Virtues Established; Justice in the Individual Confirmed

elements.context: τῷ τὸ ἑαυτοῦ ἕκαστον ἐν αὐτῇ πράττειν
δίκαιός τε ἔσται καὶ τὰ αὑτοῦ πράττων
μὴ ἐάσαντα τἀλλότρια πράττειν ἕκαστον ἐν αὑτῷ

signals.observation: The phrase τὰ αὑτοῦ πράττειν recurs densely across the section as the defining formula for justice; at 443d τἀλλότρια πράττειν appears as its explicit opposite.

elements.context: οὐ περὶ τὴν ἔξω πρᾶξιν τῶν αὑτοῦ

signals.observation: Justice is explicitly redirected from ἔξω to ἐντός, a spatial contrast between outer action and inner relation.

A cluster from the ἁρμονία word-family: ἁρμονίᾳ in the context of taming the spirited part, then συναρμόσαντα, ἁρμονίας, and ἡρμοσμένον in the musical-harmonic image of the three soul-parts bound together.

elements.form: νεάτης τε καὶ ὑπάτης καὶ μέσης
elements.context: ὥσπερ ὅρους τρεῖς ἁρμονίας ἀτεχνῶς, νεάτης τε καὶ ὑπάτης καὶ μέσης

signals.observation: The three soul-parts are compared to three notes of a musical scale—lowest, highest, and middle—an explicit simile introducing concrete musical terminology.

elements.context: καταδουλώσασθαι καὶ ἄρχειν ἐπιχειρήσῃ ὧν οὐ προσῆκον αὐτῷ γένει

signals.observation: ἄρχειν first belongs properly to the rational part, then is seized improperly by the appetitive, then is agreed upon unanimously in temperance, then becomes reflexive self-rule (ἄρξαντα αὐτὸν αὑτοῦ).

elements.context: τὸν ἰδιώτην καὶ τούτῳ σοφὸν εἶναι
σώφρονα οὐ τῇ φιλίᾳ καὶ συμφωνίᾳ

signals.observation: The four virtues—σοφόν, ἀνδρεῖος, δίκαιος, σώφρων—are transferred in sequence from city to individual.

elements.context: τέλεον ἄρα ἡμῖν τὸ ἐνύπνιον ἀποτετέλεσται

signals.observation: Justice's discovery is framed through ἐνύπνιον (dream) and εἴδωλον (image/phantom), both naming something short of full reality.

elements.context: τέλεον ἄρα ἡμῖν τὸ ἐνύπνιον ἀποτετέλεσται

signals.observation: A past suspicion (ὑποπτεῦσαι) is declared completed (ἀποτετέλεσται), with τέλεον and ἀποτετέλεσται sharing the τελ- root.

elements.context: παρακαταθήκην χρυσίου ἢ ἀργυρίου δεξάμενος… ἀποστερῆσαι

signals.observation: A catalogue of concrete injustices—embezzlement of a deposit, temple-robbery, theft, betrayal, adultery, neglect of parents, neglect of gods—is marshalled as τὰ φορτικά (vulgar tests) of the just person.
The concrete test cases are introduced with the dismissive label τὰ φορτικά (vulgar/coarse things), applied to what would ordinarily be regarded as serious moral cases.

elements.context: τῇ φιλίᾳ καὶ συμφωνίᾳ τῇ αὐτῶν τούτων

signals.observation: σύμφωνα describes what the blend of music and gymnastic produces; συμφωνίᾳ names the agreement among soul-parts that constitutes temperance.
Tightening (ἐπιτείνουσα) and relaxing (ἀνιεῖσα) are paired as opposite operations of μουσική and γυμναστική on the two soul-parts.
The just person is described as becoming entirely one out of many—a striking formulation of unity from plurality.

elements.context: τὸν μὲν σκυτοτομικὸν φύσει ὀρθῶς ἔχειν σκυτοτομεῖν

signals.observation: The shoemaker and carpenter are named as the εἴδωλον of justice—craft-specific doing-one's-own at the external level, explicitly distinguished from true justice.

elements.context: ἣ ἂν ταύτην τὴν ἕξιν σῴζῃ τε καὶ συναπεργάζηται
σοφίαν δὲ τὴν ἐπιστατοῦσαν ταύτῃ τῇ πράξει ἐπιστήμην
ἀμαθίαν δὲ τὴν ταύτῃ αὖ ἐπιστατοῦσαν δόξαν

signals.observation: A fourfold naming scheme: just action preserves (σῴζῃ) the inner ἕξις, unjust action dissolves (λύῃ) it; wisdom is ἐπιστήμη governing this, ignorance is δόξα governing its opposite.

elements.context: κατὰ θεόν τινα εἰς ἀρχήν τε καὶ τύπον τινὰ τῆς δικαιοσύνης κινδυνεύομεν ἐμβεβηκέναι

signals.observation: The initial stumbling upon justice is attributed to some god (κατὰ θεόν τινα), and what was found is called an ἀρχή and τύπος of justice.

sections.title: Injustice Defined; Virtue as Health; Five Constitutions Announced

elements.context: στάσιν τινὰ αὖ τριῶν ὄντων τούτων
ἐπανάστασιν μέρους τινὸς τῷ ὅλῳ τῆς ψυχῆς

signals.observation: Injustice is defined through a dense cluster of disorder-terms: στάσις, πολυπραγμοσύνη, ἀλλοτριοπραγμοσύνη, ἐπανάστασις, ταραχή, πλάνη, all gathered in a single sentence.

elements.context: τῷ δʼ οὐ δουλεύειν ἀρχικοῦ γένους ὄντι

signals.observation: The part whose nature is to be enslaved (δουλεύειν) is contrasted with the part that is of the ruling kind (ἀρχικοῦ γένους), and injustice is the reversal of this relation.
Four specific vices are listed then gathered under συλλήβδην πᾶσαν κακίαν.

elements.context: τὰ ἐν τῷ σώματι κατὰ φύσιν καθιστάναι
τὸ δὲ νόσον παρὰ φύσιν ἄρχειν τε καὶ ἄρχεσθαι

signals.observation: κατὰ φύσιν and παρὰ φύσιν are set in explicit contrast, first applied to body (health/disease), then repeated for soul (justice/injustice).

elements.context: κατὰ φύσιν καθιστάναι κρατεῖν τε καὶ κρατεῖσθαι ὑπʼ ἀλλήλων
παρὰ φύσιν ἄρχειν τε καὶ ἄρχεσθαι ἄλλο ὑπʼ ἄλλου

signals.observation: Health uses κρατεῖν/κρατεῖσθαι with ὑπʼ ἀλλήλων (reciprocal), while disease uses ἄρχειν/ἄρχεσθαι with ἄλλο ὑπʼ ἄλλου (non-reciprocal). The active-passive pair is parallel but the prepositional phrase shifts.

elements.context: ὡς ἐκεῖνα ἐν σώματι, ταῦτα ἐν ψυχῇ

signals.observation: The body-soul analogy is made explicit: what ὑγιεινά/νοσώδη are ἐν σώματι, δίκαια/ἄδικα are ἐν ψυχῇ.
The ὑγίεια/ὑγιεινός family recurs densely across 444c–444e, moving from analogy to identification: virtue is a kind of health of the soul.

elements.form: ὑγίειά τέ τις … καὶ κάλλος καὶ εὐεξία ψυχῆς
νόσος τε καὶ αἶσχος καὶ ἀσθένεια

signals.observation: Virtue and vice each receive a triad of bodily-aesthetic terms: ὑγίεια/κάλλος/εὐεξία vs. νόσος/αἶσχος/ἀσθένεια.
ἐμποιέω recurs as the verb linking practice to produced condition in both health and justice.

elements.context: ἐάντε λανθάνῃ ἐάντε μὴ τοιοῦτος ὤν

signals.observation: The remaining question explicitly includes the conditions of escaping notice (λανθάνῃ) and escaping punishment (μὴ διδῷ δίκην).
Glaucon calls the inquiry γελοῖον and Socrates immediately echoes the word back, conceding and yet continuing.
Socrates describes the argument as an ascent (ἀναβεβήκαμεν) to a lookout point (σκοπιά) from which one sees.

elements.context: ἅ γε δὴ καὶ ἄξια θέας

signals.observation: A cluster of seeing/showing language accompanies the transition to the five constitutions: ἴδῃς, θέας, φαίνεται, κατιδεῖν, and Glaucon's response ἕπομαι frames him as following to see.

elements.form: ἓν μὲν εἶναι εἶδος τῆς ἀρετῆς

signals.observation: Virtue has one εἶδος, vice infinitely many (ἄπειρα), but four among them are singled out as worth remembering (ἄξιον ἐπιμνησθῆναι).

elements.context: πέντε μέν … πολιτειῶν, πέντε δὲ ψυχῆς

signals.observation: Five constitution-types are announced as corresponding to five soul-types; the single good form receives two names depending on whether one or more rulers: βασιλεία or ἀριστοκρατία.

elements.context: τροφῇ τε καὶ παιδείᾳ χρησάμενος ᾗ διήλθομεν

signals.observation: The section closes by grounding the good constitution's stability in τροφή and παιδεία as previously discussed (ᾗ διήλθομεν).

elements.context: τροφῇ τε καὶ παιδείᾳ χρησάμενος ᾗ διήλθομεν

signals.observation: διέρχομαι appears twice to refer back to what has been discussed, first about justice/injustice, then about education.
